title: 第005章 阿萝泣血陈冤屈第006章 百花楼里戏恶少
lines: 夜色浓稠，山林幽深。秦夜的脚步平稳而迅捷，即使背着阿萝，穿行在崎岖不平的山路上，也几乎不发出多余的声响。他的方向感极好，依靠着原主模糊的记忆和自身对地形的敏锐判断，朝着西南方向一座矮山的山腰处寻去。
阿萝伏在他背上，最初的紧绷和僵硬早已消失，只剩下全然的依赖和疲惫。伤腿传来阵阵沉闷的胀痛，但比起刮骨疗毒时的地狱景象，已是天壤之别。她能清晰感受到秦夜背部的温暖和稳定，这让她感到一种久违的、近乎奢侈的安全感。眼皮越来越沉，意识在伤痛、疲惫和安心的矛盾感觉中逐渐模糊。
不知过了多久，秦夜停下了脚步。
“到了。”他低声道。
阿萝勉强睁开困倦的眼睛，眼前是一座倚着山壁搭建的简陋木屋。木屋不大，看起来已废弃多时，屋顶的茅草塌陷了小半，木门歪斜地挂着，窗户只剩下空洞。但比起漏风的破庙，至少能遮挡大部分风雨，也更为隐蔽。
秦夜将阿萝轻轻放在木屋门口一块相对干净的大石上，自己则上前，谨慎地推开那扇歪斜的木门。门轴发出刺耳的“吱呀”声，在寂静的山林里传得很远。秦夜皱了皱眉，手上加力，将门彻底推开，闪身进入。
木屋内一片漆黑，弥漫着灰尘和腐朽木头的气味。借着门外透进来的微弱星光，能大致看清里面的格局：一个不足方丈的空间，靠墙有一个用石头垒砌的简易灶台，上面架着一口生锈的破锅。角落里堆着些干草和烂木头，还有一个倾倒的破木架，看起来曾是床铺。地上积了厚厚的灰，有野兽的爪印和一些鸟粪。
没有活物，也没有近期人类活动的痕迹。
秦夜稍微放心，转身出来，重新背起阿萝，走进木屋，将她放在那堆还算干燥的草堆上。他快速清理出一小片地方，从包裹里取出火折子，点燃一小堆从外面捡来的枯枝。橘黄色的火光跳跃起来，驱散了黑暗和寒意，也映亮了阿萝苍白的小脸和秦夜平静的面容。
“暂时在这里落脚。”秦夜一边说，一边检查阿萝的伤腿包扎，确认没有因为颠簸而移位或渗血，“你好好休息，我去弄点水和吃的，再把这地方收拾一下。”
阿萝点点头，想说什么，但喉咙干涩，只发出一声气音。
秦夜拿出水囊，让她喝了几口。水囊里的水不多了。他拿起破锅，走出木屋，很快，外面传来隐约的溪流声。不多时，他端着半锅清水回来，将锅架在简易的石灶上，添了几根柴。
火光摇曳，木屋里渐渐有了暖意。
秦夜动作麻利，先用清水将破锅简单刷洗，重新舀了水架在火上烧。然后开始清理木屋内的积灰和杂物，将那倾倒的木架扶正，铺上厚厚一层新找来的干草，做成一个简易的床铺。又用树枝和藤蔓，勉强将那扇破门修了修，至少能关合。
阿萝默默地看着秦夜忙碌的身影。他做这些事的时候，神情专注，动作利落，没有一丝不耐或嫌弃，仿佛只是在进行最平常的工作。她的心，被一种酸涩而温暖的情绪填满。
水烧开了，秦夜拿出剩下的干粮——几个冷硬的馍馍，掰碎了泡在热水里，弄成糊状。他扶起阿萝，让她靠坐在干草堆上，一勺一勺，耐心地喂她吃。
温热、寡淡的食物糊顺着食道滑下，阿萝冰冷的身体里仿佛注入了一丝生气。她小口小口地吃着，眼泪忽然毫无征兆地掉了下来，大颗大颗地砸进碗里。
秦夜喂食的动作停了一下，看着她。
阿萝慌忙抬手去擦眼泪，却越擦越多，怎么也止不住。压抑了太久的恐惧、痛苦、委屈、仇恨，在这陌生的山林，在这简陋却安全的木屋，在这跳跃的火光中，在这个沉默却给予她新生的人面前，如同决堤的洪水，再也控制不住。
“对……对不起……秦大哥……我……我忍不住……”她抽噎着，肩膀剧烈耸动，瘦小的身体蜷缩起来，像一只受伤的幼兽。
秦夜没说话，只是放下碗，静静地看着她哭。他知道，有些情绪，堵不如疏。
阿萝的哭声起初是压抑的、细碎的，渐渐变成了嚎啕大哭，哭得撕心裂肺，哭得上气不接下气。她哭惨死的爹，哭病逝的娘，哭自己断掉的腿，哭这绝望的世道，哭那些高高在上、视人命如草芥的贵人。
“爹……爹他好惨啊……”阿萝边哭边断断续续地诉说，声音被剧烈的抽泣切割得支离破碎，“他就……就那么跪在城主府门口……磕头……求他们给个说法……我就在街角……看着……”
“那些护卫……穿着那么亮的皮甲……拿着那么长的刀……他们……他们围着我爹……笑……骂他找死……”
“我爹……他……他就是个老实打铁的……一辈子没跟人红过脸……他就想问问……为什么他女儿被马踢了……车都不停……讨个汤药费……给……给我治腿……”
“可他们……他们不听……领头的那个……脸上有疤的……一脚……就把我爹踹倒……然后……然后好几个人……用刀鞘……用脚……往我爹身上打……往头上打……”
阿萝的声音骤然拔高，充满了极致的惊恐和痛苦：“我爹……他……他开始还叫……后来……后来就没声了……血……好多血……从他头上……嘴里……流出来……流了一地……”
“他们打够了……就像踢一条死狗一样……把我爹踢到路边……看都不看一眼……走了……周围……周围的人……都躲得远远的……没人敢管……”
“我爬过去……爬过去……我爹……他……他眼睛还睁着……看着我……嘴巴在动……可……可一点声音都发不出来……他……他想抬手……摸摸我的脸……手抬到一半……就……就掉下去了……”
“他就那样……看着我……咽气了……”
阿萝的声音已经嘶哑得不成样子，浑身颤抖得像风中的落叶，眼神空洞，仿佛又回到了那个绝望的午后，那个血淋淋的街角。
秦夜默默地听着，脸上依旧没什么表情，但眼底深处，冰寒的杀意如同深潭下的暗流，缓缓凝聚。他前世见过无数生死，听过无数惨事，但此刻听着一个花季少女，用如此破碎的声音，描述自己父亲被活活打死的场景，依然感到一股冰冷的怒意在胸中翻腾。
这不是江湖仇杀，不是势力倾轧。这是最赤裸裸的、恃强凌弱的虐杀！是对最底层生命最残忍的践踏！而施暴者，是所谓的“贵人”和“官府”！
阿萝哭得几乎脱力，声音渐渐低了下去，只剩下无意识的啜泣和颤抖。过了很久，她才继续开口，声音虚浮，像梦呓：
“街坊……王大伯他们……晚上偷偷把我爹抬回来……身上……都没一块好肉了……娘看到……当场就吐了血……昏死过去……”
“后来……娘就一病不起……家里……家里一点钱都没了……药也买不起……我去求药铺的掌柜……跪了一天……他……他给了我一包最便宜的草药……让我……让我节哀……”
“娘喝了药……也没用……她一直咳血……拉着我的手……说对不住我……说她没用……保护不了爹……也治不好我的腿……”
“前天早上……她……她忽然精神好了点……还对我笑……说想喝口热粥……我……我高兴坏了……拖着腿想去隔壁张婶家借点米……可……可我回来的时候……娘……娘她已经……没气了……”
“她手里……还攥着我爹打铁时用的……一块废铁……眼睛……也睁着……看着门口……”
阿萝不再哭了，眼泪似乎已经流干。她只是呆呆地看着跳跃的火光，眼神空洞麻木，仿佛灵魂已经随着爹娘一起死去，只剩下一具会呼吸的躯壳。
木屋里，只剩下柴火燃烧的噼啪声，和两人压抑的呼吸声。
content_en:
The night is thick and the mountains and forests are deep. Qin Ye's steps were steady and swift, making almost no unnecessary noise even when carrying A Luo on his back as he walked through the rugged mountain road. He had an excellent sense of direction. Relying on the vague memory of the original owner and his keen judgment of the terrain, he searched for the hillside of a low mountain in the southwest.
A Luo lay on his back, the initial tension and stiffness had long since disappeared, leaving only complete dependence and exhaustion. There were waves of dull swelling pain in the injured leg, but it was a far cry from the hell scene when scraping bones to treat poison. She could clearly feel the warmth and stability on Qin Ye's back, which made her feel a long-lost, almost luxurious sense of security. His eyelids became heavier and heavier, and his consciousness gradually blurred in the contradictory feelings of pain, exhaustion and relief.
After some time, Qin Ye stopped.
"We're here," he whispered.
A Luo reluctantly opened her sleepy eyes, and in front of her was a simple wooden house built against the mountain wall. The wooden house is small and looks like it has been abandoned for a long time. The thatch on the roof has collapsed in half, the wooden door hangs crookedly, and the windows are only empty. But compared to the leaky ruined temple, it can at least block most of the wind and rain, and is more hidden.
Qin Ye gently placed A'luo on a relatively clean boulder at the door of the wooden house, then stepped forward and cautiously pushed open the crooked wooden door. The door shaft made a harsh "squeak" sound, which could be heard far in the silent mountain forest. Qin Ye frowned, put more force on his hands, pushed the door completely open, and stepped in.
The cabin was dark and filled with the smell of dust and rotting wood. Through the faint starlight coming from outside the door, we can roughly see the layout inside: a space less than an abbot, with a simple stone stove against the wall, and a rusty broken pot on it. There were piles of hay and rotten wood in the corner, as well as an overturned wooden frame that looked like it had once been a bed. There was thick dust on the ground, and there were the paw prints of wild animals and some bird droppings.
There were no living creatures and no trace of recent human activity.
Qin Ye felt relieved, turned around, carried A Luo on his back again, walked into the wooden house, and placed her on the pile of dry hay. He quickly cleared a small area, took out the fire stick from the package, and lit a small pile of dead branches picked from outside. The orange fire light jumped up, dispelling the darkness and chill, and also illuminated A Luo's pale face and Qin Ye's calm face.
"Settlement here for the time being." Qin Ye said while checking the bandage of A Luo's injured leg to make sure it had not been displaced or bleeding due to the bumps. "You have a good rest, I will get some water and food, and then tidy up the place."
A Luo nodded and wanted to say something, but her throat was dry and she could only make a breathy sound.
Qin Ye took out the water bag and let her take a few sips. There is not much water left in the water bladder. He picked up the broken pot and walked out of the wooden house. Soon, there was a faint sound of stream outside. Not long after, he came back with a half-pot of water, placed the pot on the simple stone stove, and added some firewood.
The firelight flickered, and there was gradually warmth in the wooden house.
Qin Ye moved quickly. He briefly washed the broken pot with clean water, then scooped out water and put it on the fire. Then he began to clean up the dust and debris in the wooden house, straightened the fallen wooden frame, and spread a thick layer of newly found hay to make a simple bed. Then he used branches and vines to repair the broken door, at least it could be closed.
A Luo looked at Qin Ye's busy figure silently. When he did these things, he looked focused and moved neatly, without a trace of impatience or disgust, as if he was just doing the most ordinary work. Her heart was filled with a sour and warm emotion.
After the water boiled, Qin Ye took out the remaining dry food - a few cold and hard steamed buns, broke them into pieces, soaked them in hot water, and made them into a paste. He lifted A'luo up, let her sit on the hay, and patiently fed her spoonful by spoonful.
The warm, bland food paste slid down the esophagus, and A Luo's cold body seemed to be injected with a trace of life. She ate in small bites, and tears suddenly fell down without warning, and fell into the bowl in large pieces.
Qin Ye stopped feeding for a moment and looked at her.
Ah Luo hurriedly raised her hand to wipe away her tears, but she wiped more and more tears and couldn't stop them. The fear, pain, grievance, and hatred that had been suppressed for too long, in this unfamiliar forest, in this simple but safe wooden house, in this jumping firelight, in front of this silent person who gave her new life, were like a flood that broke a dam and could no longer be controlled.
"Yes... I'm sorry... Brother Qin... I... I can't help it..." She sobbed, her shoulders shrugged violently, and her thin body curled up like a wounded cub.
Qin Ye didn't say anything, just put down the bowl and watched her cry quietly. He knows that some emotions are better blocked than cleared.
A Luo's cries were suppressed and tinny at first, but gradually turned into howling, heartbreaking, and breathless. She cried for her father who died tragically, for her mother who died of illness, for her broken leg, for the hopeless world, and for those noble people who looked upon human lives as nothing but trivial matters.
"Dad...Dad, he is so miserable..." A Luo cried intermittently, her voice cut into pieces by the violent sobs, "He just...knelt at the door of the City Lord's Mansion...kowtow...begging them for an explanation...I was on the corner of the street...watching..."
"Those guards... wore such bright leather armor... held such long knives... they... they surrounded my father... laughed... and scolded him for seeking death..."
"My father...he...he is an honest blacksmith...he has never been embarrassed by anyone in his life...he just wanted to ask...why his daughter was kicked by a horse...the car stopped...to ask for money for soup and medicine...here...treat my leg..."
"But they...they didn't listen...the leader...the one with the scar on his face...kicked my dad down...then...then several people...hit my dad with their scabbards...with their feet...hit my dad on the head..."
A'luo's voice suddenly rose in pitch, full of extreme panic and pain: "My dad... he... he screamed at first... then... then he stopped making noise... blood... a lot of blood... flowed out from his head... mouth... and flowed all over the floor..."
"They had beaten enough...just like kicking a dead dog...kicked my dad to the side of the road...without even looking at him...and left...everyone around...kept far away...no one dared to care..."
"I crawled over... crawled over... my dad... he... his eyes were still open... looking at me... his mouth was moving... but... he couldn't make any sound... he... he wanted to raise his hand... to touch my face... he raised his hand halfway... and then... fell..."
"He just... looked at me... and died..."
A'luo's voice was hoarse, her whole body was shaking like fallen leaves in the wind, her eyes were empty, as if she had returned to that desperate afternoon, that bloody street corner.
Qin Ye listened silently, his face still expressionless, but deep in his eyes, the cold murderous intent slowly gathered like an undercurrent under a deep pool. He had seen countless lives and deaths in his previous life, and heard countless tragic events, but now when he listened to a young girl describing the scene of her father being beaten to death in such a broken voice, he still felt a cold anger boiling in his chest.
This is not a vendetta or a conflict of forces. This is the most naked, bullying and killing! It is the most cruel trampling on the lowest life! And the perpetrators are the so-called "nobles" and "officials"!
A Luo almost lost her strength from crying, and her voice gradually dropped, leaving only unconscious sobbing and trembling. After a long time, she continued to speak, her voice was hollow, like talking in sleep:
"The neighbors... Uncle Wang and the others... secretly carried my dad back at night... not a single piece of meat was left on his body... When my mother saw... she vomited blood on the spot... and passed out..."
"Later... my mother couldn't afford to fall ill... the family... the family had no money at all... and couldn't afford medicine... I went to beg the drugstore shopkeeper... I knelt for a day... he... he gave me a pack of the cheapest herbal medicine... to let me... let me grieve..."
"My mother drank the medicine...it didn't work...she kept coughing up blood...she held my hand...and said she was sorry...that she was useless...she couldn't protect dad...and she couldn't heal my leg..."
"The morning before yesterday... she... she suddenly felt better... and smiled at me... and said she wanted to drink hot porridge... I... I was so happy... I dragged my legs to go to Aunt Zhang's house next door to borrow some rice... but... but when I came back... mother... mother, she was already... out of breath..."
"In her hand... she was still holding a piece of scrap metal that my father used to make blacksmiths... her eyes... were also open... looking at the door..."
A Luo stopped crying and her tears seemed to have dried up. She just stared blankly at the dancing firelight, her eyes hollow and numb, as if her soul had died along with her parents, leaving only a breathing body.
In the wooden house, only the crackling sound of firewood and the suppressed breathing of the two people were left.
title_en: Chapter 005 A Luo weeps and grievances Chapter 006 The villain in Baihua Tower
